title: Founder build-log (Day 6): build a Stripe webhook endpoint with duplicate-event (idempotency) handling and test it locally through an ngrok tunnel

tools.name: Stripe Webhooks
tools.detail: Read the webhook docs to enumerate needed events

tools.name: ngrok
tools.detail: Public URL tunnelling to the local API so Stripe can send real payloads without deploying

claims: Stripe may send duplicate events, so the endpoint needs logic to avoid taking the same action twice
ngrok lets Stripe hit a local webhook with real payloads without deploying
how_to_steps: Read the Stripe webhook documentation and list the events you need
Build the webhook endpoint, including de-duplication so duplicate events do not re-trigger actions
Run ngrok to expose the local API; point Stripe's webhook at the ngrok URL and test with real payloads
Next: build the dashboard and the backend API powering it
on_screen_only: Karaoke captions only ('FOUNDER SERIES', 'MY 9 TO 5', 'WEBHOOK DOCUMENTATION', 'DUPLICATE EVENTS', 'I'M USING NGROK', 'LOCAL API', 'WITH REAL PAYLOAD')
Dark multi-monitor desk with an editor and the Stripe docs; no readable code

relevance.why: Payments plumbing is table stakes for Haji's apps; idempotent webhook handling and local tunnel testing are the two things vibe-coders most often skip.

implement_score.why: Add to the app-template checklist: store processed Stripe event IDs (idempotency), verify signatures, test via ngrok or 'stripe listen --forward-to'. An hour per app; no new tool to buy.

verify: Stripe CLI's 'stripe listen' can forward events locally without ngrok -- is ngrok still needed?
Confirm current Stripe guidance on event de-duplication (event.id storage) and signature verification

gap.what: New (minor) technique: idempotent Stripe webhook handling + ngrok local testing. Liked set has no payments-integration content.
